v1_blocker.finding: GOES-16 SGPS operational L2 daily files expose 1-500 MeV differential proton channels plus a >500 MeV integral channel; they do not directly expose the >=10 MeV integral quantity required by V1. Two fixed-day SGPS files were also absent even though the year directories exist.
v1_blocker.mutation_rule: V1 is preserved as a negative source-readiness result. V2 is a separately named study and may not relabel the >500 MeV channel as >=10 MeV or reinterpret the V1 failure as a pass.

target.positive_definition: At least one official NOAA/SWPC >=10 MeV, >=10 pfu proton-event onset occurs in (issue_time, issue_time+24h].
target.active_interval_definition: [official_event_start, official_event_end] using NOAA/SWPC event records; no proxy duration is allowed.
target.event_start_source: NOAA/NCEI Solar Proton Events Affecting the Earth Environment list (1976-present)
target.event_end_source: Archived NOAA/SWPC post-event summaries in Space Weather Highlights/PRF or SGAS products that explicitly state the event end/drop-below-threshold time.

historical_predictor_interval.reason: Keep one satellite and one calibration regime for the development study; preserve source gaps instead of outcome-dependent stitching.

required_variables_or_semantics: XRS-A and XRS-B irradiance/flux variables identifiable from metadata

proton_predictors.product: GOES-R SEISS SGPS L2 1-minute operational averages
required_variables_or_semantics: AvgDiffProtonFlux or an equivalently documented 1-500 MeV differential proton-flux tensor
documented lower/upper/effective energies for the differential channels
forbidden_as_v2_predictor: retrospectively reconstructed >=10 MeV integral proton flux
the >500 MeV integral SGPS channel relabelled as >=10 MeV
cross-satellite fill chosen after inspecting labels

live_products.compatibility_rule: Live readiness requires the public primary feeds to expose XRS flux and differential-proton energy/flux/time fields. The current live satellite identity does not rewrite the historical GOES-16 cohort.

label_products.event_definition_reference: NOAA/SWPC defines the start as the threshold crossing at >=10 MeV and 10 pfu and the end as the last time the >=10 MeV flux is at or above 10 pfu.
label_products.training_gate: Every event onset inside the historical predictor interval must be paired with one authoritative end time before labels are generated.

source_readiness_probe.anchor_selection_rule: For each frozen month, inspect the archive listing and choose the lexicographically first operational daily file. This uses directory metadata only and is independent of event labels.
must_verify: XRS operational files remain retrievable and carry the required XRS/time/quality semantics
SGPS operational archive exposes documented differential-proton channels with energy metadata and quality information
the NOAA event catalogue is retrievable and states the official start/end threshold semantics
at least two archived NOAA/SWPC post-event reports explicitly contain proton-event end/drop-below-threshold times
live XRS, live differential-proton, and instrument-routing JSON endpoints have non-empty machine-readable schemas
no training, label derivation, forecast scoring, or protected-outcome access occurs during source readiness

requirements: complete coverage inventory across the historical interval using filenames/timestamps only
complete event start/end interval table for every NOAA/SWPC event onset inside the interval
event intervals are non-overlapping after applying the official SWPC event definition or ambiguities are explicitly marked and excluded
chronological fit/calibration/threshold/score boundaries are frozen before model probabilities are inspected
minimum fit-role positive onsets >= 10; otherwise report INSUFFICIENT_SUPPORT and stop

claim_boundary: V2 corrects the source semantics exposed by the V1 failure. Passing source readiness only demonstrates that the causal predictor and official-label interfaces are technically usable. It does not establish model skill, independent superiority, company benefit, or operational certification.
